main_body: Small cottage building with pitched terracotta tile roof, timber-framed plaster front wall, stone foundation, wooden door, and shuttered window
top_band: Sloping terracotta tile roof from row 2 to row 43 (lighter checkered ridge/upper slope rows 3-8, main tiled slope rows 9-42, dark front eave edge row 43)
evidence: The building shows a large foreshortened top/sloping roof surface (rows 2-43) overhanging a vertical front wall (rows 44-78). Row 43 forms the distinct dark front eave edge of the roof, and rows 44-45 on the plaster wall directly beneath it are shaded with a 2px eave shadow and horizontal overhang of 2px on each side. The front door is clearly recessed inside a stone arch frame with darker inner shadow rows (53-54), and the window panes are inset behind the brown muntins/frame.

style.evidence: While the candidate avoids flat fills by sprinkling noise dots on the plaster and using 4-5 ramp steps on the roof tiles, its surface craft and structural richness are noticeably simpler than the Beodeul house references. The roof is a plain rectangle with wide, boxy brick-like tile courses rather than the intricately scalloped, high-contrast individual tiles and angled gable/hip geometry of the references. The timber framing lacks diagonal bracing or wood grain, the door is drawn with simple vertical stripes and flat grey bars, and the bright cyan window with diagonal white streaks reads much more simplistic/cartoonish than the reference buildings.
